clue.text: One looking after passengers on stairs?

definitions.text: One looking after passengers on stairs?

parts.words: One looking after passengers on stairs?
parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs as well as an aeroplane journey, so an attendant on a flight sounds like someone tending a staircase

explanation.surface: Someone helping travellers up and down a staircase, perhaps at a station.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'flight' means both a run of stairs and a plane journey; the cabin crew member is pictured on a staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabin crew on an aircraft look after the travellers aboard, serving and keeping them safe.

clue.text: Touch small metal spike, one of a few we have to hand

definitions.text: one of a few we have to hand

parts.note: to finger something is to touch it
a nail is a small metal pin hammered into wood

explanation.surface: Touching a tiny tack, one from a handful kept nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hand' sounds like 'available'; literally, the ten horny plates are on our hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Each person has ten of these horny plates at the fingertips, literally on the hand.

clue.text: News being made

definitions.meaning: facts or reports, much as news is
read as two words, ... describes something still taking shape

explanation.definitionFit: Information means knowledge or reports passed on; split up, it says something is still forming.

clue.text: Bit of a laugh before unknown excitement causes irritation

indicators.note: only part of the laugh is kept, half of its repeated syllable dropped

parts.note: ha-ha is the written sound of a laugh
the letters removed are the second half of the doubled laugh
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra
fever can mean nervous excitement, as in a fever of anticipation

explanation.surface: A giggle followed by mysterious agitation brings annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of' trims HAHA to HA; 'causes' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hay fever is an allergy to pollen that brings sneezing and itchy eyes, an irritation of the nose.

clue.text: A job so variable leads to abandonment of principles

parts.note: a post is a job or position
as can mean so, as in 'as I said'
Y is a variable in algebra

explanation.surface: A changeable occupation makes someone give up their beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable' looks like an anagram signal, but it is Y, an algebra variable.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostasy is renouncing one's religion or political creed.

clue.text: Attempt to include last part at the forefront of fashion

indicators.note: the word for attempt takes the other piece within it

parts.note: an attempt is a try
the end is the last part of anything

explanation.surface: Trying to get the final section into the latest look.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable, following the newest style.

clue.text: Extra with which cricket cannot be played

definitions.meaning: in cricket a ... is an illegal delivery giving a run to the batting side, one of the extras

definitions.text: with which cricket cannot be played
definitions.meaning: taken literally, with ... there is nothing to play cricket with

explanation.definitionFit: An illegal delivery in cricket adds a penalty run, which is counted among the extras; read literally it means the ball is absent.

clue.text: Somewhat scrawny beard

indicators.note: only some of the word scrawny is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A rather thin, wispy beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beard' is the botanical sense: the bristles on barley or wheat.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is a bristle on an ear of cereal grass; collectively these are called the beard.

clue.text: Captured also with king

parts.note: too means also
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Seized, and the monarch too.
explanation.definitionFit: Took is the past tense of take, which can mean seize or capture.

clue.text: Area where those normally going up are grounded

definitions.text: Area where those normally going up are grounded

parts.words: Area where those normally going up are grounded
parts.note: aircraft normally take off, but over this stretch of territory they are kept on the ground, like a child being punished

explanation.surface: Somewhere children who usually go upstairs are punished by being grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounded' suggests a punishment for teenagers; here it means aircraft kept from flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspace in which flights are banned, often imposed by military or international order.

clue.text: Prohibit Joanna getting instrument

parts.note: to prohibit is to ban
Jo is a short form of the name Joanna

explanation.surface: Someone stops Joanna from receiving a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joanna' is also rhyming slang for a piano, which tempts a solver to think of keyboards; here it is just the name shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed musical instrument with a round drum-like body.

clue.text: Serious notice in front of shelter

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention, so ear stands for notice or heed
a nest is a bird's shelter or a snug refuge

explanation.surface: A grave sign posted outside a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes someone sincere and grave in intention, not joking.

clue.text: American settler's anguish, we hear

indicators.note: says the word for anguish is spoken, and the answer matches its sound

parts.note: dolour is a literary word for grief or anguish

explanation.surface: The suffering of a pioneer in America, as reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settler' pictures a pioneer, but it is something that settles a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The US currency unit is what settles a debt in America, so it is a playful payer of accounts.

clue.text: Drink that could make lad emotional, losing head

indicators.note: says these letters could be formed into something else, a rearrangement
the word emotional drops its first letter

explanation.surface: A drink that might bring a young man to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts EMOTIONAL to MOTIONAL; 'could make' then rearranges LAD and MOTIONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a medium-dry Spanish sherry, a fortified wine.

clue.text: Dismal revolutionary beginning to explore London area for dolcelatte?

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling dismal
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: SE is the south-east London postcode area

explanation.surface: A gloomy rebel starts touring part of London looking for Italian cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolcelatte is a soft Italian cheese with blue-green veins of mould, an example of the type, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Some outline area starting in south-west Asia

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a sketch of a region begins in south-west Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Near East is the older name for the lands of the eastern Mediterranean and south-west Asia.

clue.text: Fleece that might be pulled over one's eyes

definitions.meaning: a sheep's fleece is its coat of ...

definitions.text: that might be pulled over one's eyes
definitions.meaning: to pull the ... over someone's eyes is to deceive them

explanation.surface: A con trick that blinds the victim.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep's coats are shorn for yarn, and the deception idiom names the same stuff.

clue.text: Fellow mostly handing out something stringy?

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: doling is handing out, as in doling out

explanation.surface: A man distributing something fibrous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stringy' suggests tough meat; it is an instrument with strings.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandolin is a lute-like instrument with paired metal strings, so a stringed thing.

clue.text: Sets apart site also disintegrating

indicators.note: falling to pieces, so the letters of site and also break up and re-form

explanation.surface: A location crumbles and is cut off as well.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate something from others, keeping it alone.

clue.text: Bit of a looker?

parts.note: a looker is slang for an attractive person, but read literally it is an eye, and one part of the eye is the coloured ring around the pupil

explanation.surface: Someone describing a rather attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of a looker' is a compliment; read literally it is a part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured ring around the pupil is one component of the eye, the organ that looks.

clue.text: One case or another outside burrow

indicators.note: the letters for another case go around the burrow

parts.note: another case, so the word case is used a second time
a sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: Choosing between two boxes kept outside an animal's den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for a second CASE, which wraps SETT, a badger's burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape cassette is a small plastic housing holding magnetic tape, so it is a sort of container.

clue.text: Wave, one can make other waves

definitions.meaning: a hair ... is used to put waves or curls in hair

explanation.definitionFit: A big breaker rolling in from the sea, and a curler that sets curls in hair.

clue.text: State half of worthless people will come up in the morning

indicators.note: the piece goes inside the abbreviation for morning

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for the morning, ante meridiem

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards
just the first half of the word for the rabble is taken

parts.note: riff-raff are disreputable or worthless people

explanation.surface: A claim that half the rabble will rise early.
explanation.walkthrough: RIFF, half of RIFFRAFF, 'will come up' as FFIR and goes 'in' AM.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to declare or assert something firmly as true.

clue.text: Specially made unit of furniture? Just the first

parts.note: one is the unit number

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word furniture is taken

explanation.surface: A bespoke piece of furniture, the first of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit of furniture' looks like a cupboard; it is ONE, OF, and the F that begins 'furniture'.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is a single item made for a particular occasion, not mass-produced.

clue.text: Temptress the French found in New Delhi

indicators.note: the French article is placed inside the rearranged city
new means the letters of Delhi are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: A seductress turns up in the Indian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' reads as part of the city's name, but it is the anagram signal, giving DELIH for 'found in' to take LA.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Delilah seduced Samson and betrayed him, so her name means a treacherous seductress.

clue.text: Behead mollusc for pound

indicators.note: behead means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the squid is a mollusc

explanation.surface: Decapitating a sea creature to hammer it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' is not a verb; QUID is British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Quid is British slang for one pound sterling.

clue.text: As far as new unit by lake

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of unit are made into a fresh order

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A fresh building block extends right up to the lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives UNTI; 'by' only places L beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Until marks a limit in time, like 'up to' a point.

clue.text: Regularly thump ram

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of thump is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Thump a male sheep at intervals, or keep ramming something.
explanation.definitionFit: A tup is a male sheep, a word used in northern England and Scotland.

clue.text: Uncomfortable, unwell but relaxing

parts.note: to be unwell is to be ill
at ease means relaxed, in the military command sense of standing at rest

explanation.surface: Someone sick yet trying to unwind, and failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill at ease describes someone awkward or uneasy in a situation.

clue.text: Leave fellows having time with stock for large shop

parts.note: to leave is to depart
fellows are men
a store is a stock or supply

explanation.surface: Men quit their jobs with time and goods for a big retailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A large retail building divided into sections each selling a different range of goods.
